about.title: Live Oak Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Live Oak sits along a stretch of Sutter County where Rt 99 carries steady traffic through town, crossing paths with local roads like Pennington Road and Larkin Road. Public collision records show injury crashes here tend to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., often tied to commuter and agricultural traffic converging on these corridors. Even a town this size sees real consequences from these collisions — torn ligaments, fractured bones, and lingering pain that outlasts the initial ER visit. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, sorting out fault, medical bills, and insurance calls can feel like a second job on top of recovering. We handle personal injury claims and can review what happened, explain your options in plain terms, and work your case on contingency. There's no cost to find out where you stand.
commonInjuries: Concussion or mild traumatic brain injury

whyChoose.title: Why Live Oak Drivers Choose Us

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file suit, but if a government vehicle or road defect on Rt 99 or Pennington Road was involved, that window can shrink to six months. We help make sure that deadline doesn't slip by unnoticed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you're partly at fault, with your share reducing the total rather than eliminating it. Our team can help make sure the insurer isn't assigning you more blame than the facts support.

items.title: Skip the Recorded Statement Trap
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement right after a crash, hoping to lock in words that limit your claim later. We can speak for you and help preserve evidence before it disappears.

items.question: I was hurt on Rt 99 near Live Oak but I'm not sure who was at fault. Can I still get help?
items.answer: Yes. California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash. We can review the police report and any witness accounts from the scene to help sort out how fault should be divided.

items.question: How long do I have to take action after a Live Oak crash?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That window can be much shorter — sometimes just six months — if a government entity, like a road maintenance agency, may be responsible. It's worth having a conversation sooner rather than later so evidence and deadlines don't work against you.

items.question: Does your firm charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews — there's no charge to discuss your situation. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
